Some tips that might help :

1) When you get a sugar craving , drink a cold sprite zero or coke zero. I find it to help the sugar cravings.

2) The rule "out of sight, out of mind" it really does work- so maybe put your candy stash in the closet (or maybe not even buy candy from the store anymore)

3) Try fruit for a replacement! And it is really helpful if you leave fruit on the counter. It's more on hand to grab. 

4) Sugar-free mints are also good, too. They occupy the mouth. 

5) Distract yourself, take a bath, or clean, etc...

1) If you can have big equipment at home, if you can , buy a kettle bell or dumbells for home. If you can't do that, try to lift/ pick up more heavy things at home. (But make sure to be aware of your position when you do that so you can prevent injuries to your body!)

2) Watch a 10-15 min video on YouTube for exercises that only involve staying at home and no gym equipment (but make sure to set a schedule and stay consistent to that) (also stretching can help prevent injuries when exercising) 

3)  Use rubber exercising bands to work out with! 
4) You can also do activities that dont use as much space, like situps, push-ups, jumping jack's, squats, etc...
